question: do reported earnings and cash reflect economic reality?

earnings_versus_cash.finding: Over the trailing four quarters operating cash flow is {earnings_versus_cash.operating_cash_flow_over_net_income.value} times net income, against {earnings_versus_cash.history.years.0.operating_cash_flow_over_net_income} in fiscal 2025, {earnings_versus_cash.history.years.1.operating_cash_flow_over_net_income} in fiscal 2024 and {earnings_versus_cash.history.years.2.operating_cash_flow_over_net_income} in fiscal 2023. The ratio widened because trailing net income changed by {ratios.growth.net_income.trailing_four_quarters.value|pct} while trailing operating cash flow changed by {ratios.growth.operating_cash_flow.trailing_four_quarters.value|pct}. In the third quarter of fiscal 2026 alone net income was {ratios.growth.net_income.this_quarter.value} against operating cash flow of {ratios.growth.operating_cash_flow.this_quarter.value}, the calculator's quarter figure being the year-to-date statement less the half-year statement. Accruals over average assets are {earnings_versus_cash.accruals_over_average_assets.value}, against {trend_table.years-back-0.ratios.accruals_over_total_assets.value} in fiscal 2025, {trend_table.years-back-1.ratios.accruals_over_total_assets.value} in fiscal 2024 and {trend_table.years-back-4.ratios.accruals_over_total_assets.value} in fiscal 2021, so cash has run ahead of earnings in every filled year and the current reading sits inside that range; the average-assets denominator mixes a balance sheet before CyberArk with one after it. The gap between cash and income is non-cash charges, share-based compensation of {terms.trailing_four_quarters.share_based_compensation.value} and depreciation and amortization of {terms.trailing_four_quarters.depreciation_and_amortization.value} over the trailing four quarters, plus billings collected ahead of revenue. Receivables rose {earnings_versus_cash.working_capital.receivables.balance_sheet_change.value} on the balance sheet year over year, {earnings_versus_cash.working_capital.receivables.share_of_net_income.value} times trailing net income, while the cash-flow statement's receivables line over the trailing four quarters records {earnings_versus_cash.working_capital.receivables.cash_flow_statement_change.value}, an articulation gap of {earnings_versus_cash.working_capital.receivables.articulation_gap.value}. Receivables acquired with CyberArk and Koi would produce a gap in that direction, because acquired balances enter through the acquisition and not through the operating line, but no item in my input states the acquired receivables, so the gap is unresolved. Payables rose {earnings_versus_cash.working_capital.accounts_payable.balance_sheet_change.value}, only {earnings_versus_cash.working_capital.accounts_payable.share_of_net_income.value} times trailing net income, with an articulation gap of {earnings_versus_cash.working_capital.accounts_payable.articulation_gap.value}, so payables are not funding the cash flow. Inventory cannot be tested: no inventory is tagged at any quarter end, so its working-capital change and articulation gap are missing from calculator_filings_only.json. Smoothness is {earnings_versus_cash.smoothness.value}, below one, so quarterly income moves less than quarterly operating cash flow; the cash series swings with first-quarter collections, as in the first quarter of fiscal 2026 at {earnings_versus_cash.smoothness.operating_cash_flow.2}, and the quarterly accrual metric is filled in too few quarters to support a trend.
earnings_versus_cash.verdict: Earnings are backed by cash: operating cash flow runs well ahead of net income, inside the company's own historical range, and no working-capital build is funding it. The open point is the receivables articulation gap, most plausibly acquired balances but not confirmed in the input.

revenue_recognition.finding: Days sales outstanding for the third quarter of fiscal 2026 is {trend_table.quarters-back-0.ratios.days_sales_outstanding.value}, the highest of the filled quarters, against {trend_table.quarters-back-1.ratios.days_sales_outstanding.value} in the prior quarter and {trend_table.quarters-back-4.ratios.days_sales_outstanding.value} a year earlier, and receivables over quarter revenue is at its high too, {trend_table.quarters-back-0.ratios.receivables_over_revenue.value} against {trend_table.quarters-back-4.ratios.receivables_over_revenue.value} a year earlier. Quarter-end receivables are {terms.balances_now.receivables.value} against {terms.balances_a_year_earlier.receivables.value} a year earlier, while quarter revenue grew {ratios.growth.revenue.year_over_year.value|pct}; on the calculator's trailing average-balance basis DSO is {ratios.efficiency.days_sales_outstanding.value}. A benign reading exists, since CyberArk's receivables entered the balance sheet in full while only part of a quarter of its revenue sits in the denominator, and the notes put the acquired businesses at "revenue of $388 million and $391 million" for the three and nine months; no item explains the receivables level, so the reading is unconfirmed. Contract liabilities move the other way: current deferred revenue over quarter revenue is {trend_table.quarters-back-0.ratios.contract_liabilities_over_revenue.value}, the lowest of the filled quarters, against {trend_table.quarters-back-4.ratios.contract_liabilities_over_revenue.value} a year earlier, even though the CyberArk allocation added assumed deferred revenue, and the cash-flow line for the change in deferred revenue is smaller in the first nine months of fiscal 2026 than a year earlier (item revenue_recognition_fact_contract_liabilities_change_in_cash_flow). Receivables at a high and deferred revenue at a low against revenue in the same quarter is the pattern of revenue recognised faster than it is billed ahead, and it coincides with a new judgment area: MD&A now says "our product revenue also includes on-premise software licenses of certain identity security offerings", recognised on delivery of the license, so part of the acquired revenue is recognised at a point in time. Growth is now attributed partly to acquisitions, "Our growth reflects the increased adoption of our portfolio, which consists of product, subscriptions, and support, and our recent acquisitions", and the company says "we may qualitatively or quantitatively disclose the impact of our acquisitions on revenue, costs, and expenses for the one year period subsequent to the acquisition date where such discussions would be meaningful", so the organic rate is reported at management's discretion. At fiscal year ends the receivables measure fell from {trend_table.years-back-3.ratios.days_sales_outstanding.value} in fiscal 2022 to {trend_table.years-back-0.ratios.days_sales_outstanding.value} in fiscal 2025, so the quarter's high is not part of a multi-year build. Fourth-quarter revenue concentration cannot be tested, because the record has no fiscal fourth-quarter cell and the fourth-quarter derivation is not in my input. No item mentions extended payment terms, bill-and-hold, variable consideration, principal-versus-agent or standalone-selling-price changes.
revenue_recognition.verdict: Watch, leaning adverse until explained: receivables at a quarterly high and deferred revenue at a quarterly low against revenue, alongside a new point-in-time license stream; acquisition timing is a credible benign reading that the input does not confirm.

estimates_and_reserves.finding: The allowance for doubtful accounts over gross receivables is {trend_table.quarters-back-0.ratios.bad_debt_reserve_ratio.value|pct}, the lowest of the filled quarters, against {trend_table.quarters-back-1.ratios.bad_debt_reserve_ratio.value|pct} in the prior quarter and {trend_table.quarters-back-4.ratios.bad_debt_reserve_ratio.value|pct} a year earlier; the allowance balance is {terms.balances_now.bad_debt_allowance.value} against {terms.balances_a_year_earlier.bad_debt_allowance.value} a year earlier, and it fell within the quarter in which receivables peaked (item estimates_and_discretion_fact_allowance_for_doubtful_accounts). Fair-value accounting for acquired receivables dilutes the ratio but does not lower the balance, and no item explains the fall; the only related text says of a coming credit-loss expedient "We do not expect the adoption of this standard will have a material impact on our consolidated financial statements". On contingent consideration the company says "we reduced our estimate of future cash payments" under the QRadar arrangement, booking "a gain of $110 million for the change in fair value of contingent consideration liability" inside general and administrative expense, and the cash-flow remeasurement line turns from a charge a year earlier to a credit (item estimates_and_discretion_fact_contingent_consideration_remeasurement). That estimate change raises reported income; no field in calculator_filings_only.json carries its amount, so no earnings adjustment is written for it. Inventory and warranty reserve ratios are empty in every period because the record tags neither reserve, while MD&A says product cost rose "partially offset by a decrease in inventory excess and obsolete charges" and also cites "supply chain disruptions, including increased memory, storage or other component shortages"; the inventory write-down field is missing for the current year to date, so the reserve change cannot be sized. The largest CyberArk intangible, platform renewals, carries a long useful life (item estimates_and_discretion_cyberark_platform_renewals_long_useful_life), which spreads amortization thinly, and the allocations stay open, "which may result in changes to the amounts and allocations recorded"; no goodwill impairment test, headroom, discount rate or growth assumption is in my input. The surrendered convertible notes are a current liability "estimated based on the sum of the daily conversion values computed from our stock price" over a window running past the balance-sheet date, and under the newly elected fair value option "changes in fair value of 2030 Notes included in earnings were a loss of $37 million", so earnings now move with the share price. Taxes run against the company, not for it: the note says "our provision for income taxes reflected an effective tax rate of negative" for the quarter, year-to-date tax expense of {terms.trailing_four_quarters.income_tax_expense.parts.this_year_to_date.value} compares with {terms.trailing_four_quarters.income_tax_expense.parts.prior_year_to_date.value} a year earlier on lower pre-tax income, the trailing effective rate is {tax_rate.effective_rate|pct}, and the deferred income tax line swings from a large non-cash benefit in the prior-year nine months to a small charge (item estimates_and_discretion_fact_deferred_income_taxes); no valuation-allowance release lifts the quarter. For CyberArk "Substantially all of goodwill is deductible for U.S. income tax purposes", so cash taxes should run below book tax later. The base year carried a partial release of the Centripetal litigation accrual (item earnings_quality_general_and_administrative_drivers_with_contingent_consideration_gain), the accrual now reads "we accrued $150 million and $146 million based on the judgment and estimated interest, which is recorded in other long-term liabilities", and the European matters carry no accrual: "Those matters are still pending".
estimates_and_reserves.verdict: Mixed: a cut to the contingent-consideration estimate adds a gain to the loss quarter, the allowance thinned to a quarterly low while receivables peaked, and inventory obsolescence charges fell without a measurable reserve; taxes and the new fair-value judgments move against reported income rather than for it.

cost_deferral.finding: No development cost is capitalised: the record tags no capitalised software additions, and research and development of {terms.trailing_four_quarters.research_and_development_expense.value} over the trailing four quarters is expensed (item earnings_quality_fact_research_and_development_expense). Capitalised contract costs are steady between the fiscal year end and the quarter end, the current part rising and the non-current part falling, while their amortization rose (items earnings_quality_fact_capitalized_contract_cost_current, earnings_quality_fact_capitalized_contract_cost_noncurrent and earnings_quality_fact_contract_cost_amortization), so deferred selling cost is not building. Prepaid expenses and other current assets rose between the year end and the quarter end (item earnings_quality_fact_prepaid_and_other_current_assets), but the cash-flow line covers current and non-current other assets together, so no articulation can be read from my input. The soft-asset share is {trend_table.quarters-back-0.ratios.soft_asset_share.value|pct}, the highest of the filled quarters, against {trend_table.quarters-back-1.ratios.soft_asset_share.value|pct} in the prior quarter and {trend_table.years-back-1.ratios.soft_asset_share.value|pct} at the fiscal 2024 year end, because CyberArk goodwill and intangibles entered the balance sheet; this is acquisition accounting rather than capitalised operating cost, but it puts impairment judgment at the centre of future earnings. Costs are being recognised rather than deferred: quarter gross margin is {trend_table.quarters-back-0.ratios.gross_margin.value|pct}, the lowest of the filled quarters, against {trend_table.quarters-back-4.ratios.gross_margin.value|pct} a year earlier, as acquired-intangible amortization enters both cost-of-revenue lines. Items presented as temporary recur: the quarter's operating result of {ratios.growth.operating_income.this_quarter.value} carries the acquired businesses' "operating loss of $523 million and $524 million", acceleration where "we recorded share-based compensation of $177 million", CyberArk transaction costs and severance, and management frames its expense outlook "Excluding the near-term impact of our recent acquisitions", yet Chronosphere, CyberArk and Koi closed within fiscal 2026 and Portkey closed after the quarter. Other income in the first nine months was lifted by "increased gains on sales of our investments to fund acquisitions", a portfolio gain rather than an operating one. The non-GAAP to GAAP gap cannot be measured, because the record carries no non-GAAP measure and no earnings-release body is in my input.
cost_deferral.verdict: No operating cost is being deferred; the concern runs the other way, with large acquisition charges framed as near-term in a year of repeated acquisitions, one-off portfolio gains in other income, and a balance sheet now dominated by soft assets.

cash_flow_engineering_and_off_balance_sh.finding: Receivables sales lift operating cash: "We sold financing receivables of $49 million and $54 million" in the three and nine months, more than in the same periods of fiscal 2025 (item liquidity_and_capital_financing_receivables_sold); I write a reducing cash-flow adjustment against terms.trailing_four_quarters.proceeds_from_sale_of_receivables, but that field is missing because the record tags no such proceeds, so Python may find no amount to apply. Both financing-receivable balances fell between the fiscal year end and the quarter end, and the operating cash-flow line for financing receivables is larger in the first nine months of fiscal 2026 than a year earlier (item revenue_recognition_fact_financing_receivables_change_in_cash_flow), while the trade-receivables line records {terms.trailing_four_quarters.change_in_receivables.parts.this_year_to_date.value} against {terms.trailing_four_quarters.change_in_receivables.parts.prior_year_to_date.value}, a smaller release than a year earlier. MD&A credits the rise in year-to-date operating cash flow, from {terms.trailing_four_quarters.operating_cash_flow.parts.prior_year_to_date.value} to {terms.trailing_four_quarters.operating_cash_flow.parts.this_year_to_date.value}, to "growth of our business as reflected by increases in collections"; the cash-flow lines show a shrinking, partly sold customer-financing book carrying part of that rise, a source that runs out rather than recurs. Contingent consideration paid to IBM sits in financing activities (item related_parties_contingencies_and_subsequent_events_fact_contingent_consideration_payments), outside operating cash flow and outside the acquisitions line that quality-adjusted free cash flow subtracts, and no calculator field carries it. Supplier finance and guarantee exposure are tagged in no period, so both calculator fields are missing, and nothing in my input describes a supplier-finance programme, a guarantee or a variable-interest entity. Purchase obligations rose to {terms.balances_now.unconditional_purchase_obligations.value} from {terms.balances_a_year_earlier.unconditional_purchase_obligations.value} a year earlier, mostly cloud hosting, and the notes add "a $92 million minimum purchase commitment with a cloud hosting service provider through September 2027 with no specified annual commitments". On leases, "The amendments resulted in an increase of $262 million in our right-of-use assets in exchange for new operating lease liabilities", yet the calculator carries an operating lease liability of {ratios.solvency.operating_lease_liability.value} from the fiscal 2025 year end because the quarter's filing tags no total, and it flags that the non-current part alone now exceeds that figure. Share-based compensation is a real cost: {terms.trailing_four_quarters.share_based_compensation.value} over the trailing four quarters against {earnings_versus_cash.history.years.0.share_based_compensation} in fiscal 2025, raised by accelerated vesting and set to stay high because "The remaining fair value was allocated to future services and will be expensed over the remaining service periods as share-based compensation". It and acquisition cash of {free_cash_flow.free_cash_flow_quality_adjusted.inputs.acquisitions.cash_spent} are already subtracted, taking quality-adjusted free cash flow to {free_cash_flow.free_cash_flow_quality_adjusted.value} against simple free cash flow of {free_cash_flow.free_cash_flow_simple.value}.
cash_flow_engineering_and_off_balance_sh.verdict: Moderate concern: part of the operating cash flow rise comes from a shrinking, partly sold customer-financing book that MD&A describes as collections; purchase commitments rose steeply off the balance sheet; share-based compensation is a large real cost, already deducted.

controls_audit_and_filing_signals.finding: The controls section states "There were no changes in our internal control over financial reporting" for the quarter in which the company consolidated CyberArk and Koi, and it says nothing about integrating the acquired businesses' controls or excluding them from the evaluation (item controls_audit_and_filings_no_control_change_reported_in_acquisition_quarter); total assets stepped up within that quarter (item structure_and_disclosure_changes_fact_total_assets), so the silence is unresolved. No material weakness, auditor change or critical audit matter appears, but a 10-Q carries no auditor's report and none was supplied. No officer departure appears: the current reports filed within the quarter are listed by item code only, under other events, with no body. The index lists no late-filing notification and no amendment is in my input. No restatement trace is in my directory and the numbers reader found no change of tag; two prior-period descriptions moved between filings, Koi's consideration (see cross-document reconciliation) and the Centripetal prior-year comparison, which is now given for different periods than the prior 10-Q used and so is not a restatement on its face (item related_parties_contingencies_and_subsequent_events_centripetal_accrual_and_interest). Related-party transactions, the subsidiary list and SEC comment letters are not in my input, so nothing is found on them.
controls_audit_and_filing_signals.verdict: No adverse control or filing signal is visible, but visibility is thin: no auditor's report, no 8-K bodies, and a controls statement silent on a very large acquisition.

cross_document_reconciliation.finding: Of the notes items that carry a direction, the numbers confirm most, covering revenue, product and subscription revenue, goodwill, amortization, share-based compensation, the cost lines, the operating loss, the tax rate, financing and investing cash flows, financing receivables, leases and property, and none is contradicted by the company's own figures; the rest are unresolved because they look to the next quarter, describe a line the calculator does not compute, or name an account my input does not carry. The notes answer the numbers reader's open question on convertible debt: the balances (items liquidity_and_capital_fact_convertible_debt_current and liquidity_and_capital_fact_convertible_debt_noncurrent) are the assumed CyberArk notes, not new borrowing, and their zero coupon explains interest expense of {terms.trailing_four_quarters.interest_expense.value}. Two contradictions sit in the pipeline rather than the filing. The calculator's total debt is {ratios.solvency.total_debt.value} because the convertible notes are tagged under concepts its debt groups do not read. The numbers reader describes the negative receivables lines in the cash-flow statement as uses of cash, whereas the calculator labels that line as the increase in the asset and both receivables balances fell, so those lines are releases of cash. On Koi, the prior 10-Q prints a consideration figure (item related_parties_contingencies_and_subsequent_events_note_koi_security_consideration) while this 10-Q says "The total purchase consideration for the acquisition of Koi was $231 million" and separately "we issued $61 million of replacement equity awards"; the bases differ and whether they reconcile is unresolved. MD&A says "our commitments to purchase products, components, cloud hosting and other services totaled $8.6 billion", above the note-table total the calculator carries at {terms.balances_now.unconditional_purchase_obligations.value}; the cloud-hosting minimum commitment stated outside the table is a candidate for the difference, which I do not compute. The notes say "In April 2026, we elected to terminate portions of the capped calls in exchange for $10 million in cash", and the only convertible-debt proceeds line carries the same amount (item liquidity_and_capital_fact_convertible_debt_proceeds), which the calculator counts as borrowing issued of {terms.cash_flow_families.borrowing_issued.value}; whether it is the same cash is unresolved. The pro forma note pairs CyberArk's calendar quarters with the company's April quarters, "with the historical results of CyberArk for the three and nine months ended March 31, 2026 and 2025, respectively", a convention rather than a discrepancy, and MD&A speaks of conversion "should the holders choose to convert their 2030 Notes during the fiscal quarter ending July 31, 2026" while the notes test conversion by calendar quarter, a wording difference with no number at stake. The 8-K earnings release cannot be checked against the 10-Q: the index lists a results-of-operations current report filed 2026-06-02 but no release body is in my input, so no release figure can be compared.
cross_document_reconciliation.verdict: The company's numbers and its explanations agree wherever both are visible; the open points are a Koi consideration that changed description between filings, an MD&A commitments total above the note table, a capped-call cash line of uncertain classification, and two pipeline readings that misstate debt and cash-flow signs.

industry_lens.finding: The company sells hardware firewalls alongside subscriptions, so the hardware questions apply to its product line. Inventory obsolescence: no inventory is tagged at any quarter end; at fiscal year ends days of inventory moved from {trend_table.years-back-1.ratios.days_sales_of_inventory.value} to {trend_table.years-back-0.ratios.days_sales_of_inventory.value}, and MD&A reports lower excess-and-obsolete charges while naming memory and storage shortages, so obsolescence risk is unmeasured and the reserve trend unresolved. Purchase commitments in excess of need: tagged obligations rose to {terms.balances_now.unconditional_purchase_obligations.value} from {terms.balances_a_year_earlier.unconditional_purchase_obligations.value} while trailing revenue grew {ratios.growth.revenue.trailing_four_quarters.value|pct}; they are mostly cloud hosting (item across_documents_purchase_commitments_total_mdna_against_note) and the input does not say how much came with CyberArk, so whether they exceed need is unresolved. Customer concentration: in fiscal 2025 the filing's distributor group held {concentration.facts.0.value|pct} of receivables and customers A, B and C held {concentration.facts.1.value|pct}, {concentration.facts.2.value|pct} and {concentration.facts.3.value|pct} of revenue; no later concentration fact is in the record. Channel stuffing: receivables at their quarterly high, receivables concentrated in distributors and product revenue up against the year-ago quarter (item revenue_recognition_fact_product_revenue) form the pattern to watch, but with no channel inventory, sell-through or quarter-end inventory data and an acquisition distorting the quarter, it is unresolved rather than found. Circular or vendor-financed deals: the company finances customers through financing receivables, a book that shrank and was partly sold; nothing in my input describes an investment in a customer that then buys from the company, so nothing found there.
industry_lens.verdict: No industry-specific distortion is found, but none can be ruled out: inventory is invisible at quarter ends, commitments rose sharply, and distributor concentration of receivables coincides with a receivables high.

No income-taxes-payable line is in my input and the deferred tax balances moved for several reasons.
No income-taxes-payable line is in my input; the effect lies in later periods.

anomalies.name: Operating cash flow far above net income, wider than in fiscal 2025 and fiscal 2024
anomalies.what: Trailing operating cash flow is {earnings_versus_cash.operating_cash_flow_over_net_income.value} times trailing net income, against {earnings_versus_cash.history.years.0.operating_cash_flow_over_net_income} in fiscal 2025 and {earnings_versus_cash.history.years.1.operating_cash_flow_over_net_income} in fiscal 2024. The widening comes from income falling, with quarter net income of {ratios.growth.net_income.this_quarter.value} against quarter operating cash flow of {ratios.growth.operating_cash_flow.this_quarter.value}. Cash is not lagging earnings; the gap is non-cash charges, of which share-based compensation is a real cost.

anomalies.name: Receivables balance change not matched by the cash-flow statement
anomalies.what: Receivables rose {earnings_versus_cash.working_capital.receivables.balance_sheet_change.value} year over year, but the cash-flow statement's receivables line over the trailing four quarters records {earnings_versus_cash.working_capital.receivables.cash_flow_statement_change.value}, leaving {earnings_versus_cash.working_capital.receivables.articulation_gap.value}. Receivables acquired with CyberArk and Koi would produce a gap in this direction, but no item states the acquired amount and no prose explains receivables.

anomalies.name: Receivables growth larger than a year of earnings
anomalies.what: The year-over-year rise in receivables is {earnings_versus_cash.working_capital.receivables.share_of_net_income.value} times trailing net income, while payables supplied only {earnings_versus_cash.working_capital.accounts_payable.share_of_net_income.value} times. Inventory cannot be measured because no quarter-end inventory is tagged.

anomalies.name: Quarterly income smoother than quarterly operating cash flow
anomalies.what: Smoothness is {earnings_versus_cash.smoothness.value}: quarter-to-quarter changes in net income vary less than those in operating cash flow. The cash series swings with first-quarter collections, as in the first quarter of fiscal 2026 at {earnings_versus_cash.smoothness.operating_cash_flow.2}, a billing pattern on its face; with one reading and no history of the measure, it stays unresolved.

anomalies.name: Days sales outstanding at its quarterly high
anomalies.what: Quarter DSO is {trend_table.quarters-back-0.ratios.days_sales_outstanding.value} against {trend_table.quarters-back-4.ratios.days_sales_outstanding.value} a year earlier and {trend_table.quarters-back-1.ratios.days_sales_outstanding.value} in the prior quarter, and receivables over quarter revenue is {trend_table.quarters-back-0.ratios.receivables_over_revenue.value} against {trend_table.quarters-back-4.ratios.receivables_over_revenue.value}; both are the highest of the filled quarters. No notes item explains receivables; acquired receivables set against a partial quarter of acquired revenue is a benign reading the input does not confirm.

anomalies.name: Deferred revenue at its quarterly low against revenue
anomalies.what: Current deferred revenue over quarter revenue is {trend_table.quarters-back-0.ratios.contract_liabilities_over_revenue.value}, the lowest of the filled quarters, against {trend_table.quarters-back-4.ratios.contract_liabilities_over_revenue.value} a year earlier, in the quarter receivables peaked. The year-to-date cash-flow line for deferred revenue is smaller than a year earlier and the balance includes deferred revenue assumed with CyberArk, so billing ahead of revenue is weaker than the balance suggests; no notes item addresses billings.

anomalies.name: New point-in-time license revenue from CyberArk
anomalies.name_ko: CyberArk 온프레미스 라이선스의 시점 인식 매출 추가
anomalies.what: MD&A now says "our product revenue also includes on-premise software licenses of certain identity security offerings", recognised on delivery of the license, a new judgment area in which revenue for multi-period license terms is recognised up front. Product revenue rose against the year-ago quarter, consistent with the prose.

anomalies.name: Acquired revenue inside reported growth, disclosed at discretion
anomalies.what: Quarter revenue grew {ratios.growth.revenue.year_over_year.value|pct} year over year, and the notes put the acquired businesses at "revenue of $388 million and $391 million" for the three and nine months. MD&A now attributes growth partly to acquisitions and reserves discretion over whether to disclose acquisition impact, so the organic rate is not a figure the company commits to report.

anomalies.name: Allowance for doubtful accounts thinned to its quarterly low
anomalies.what: The allowance over gross receivables is {trend_table.quarters-back-0.ratios.bad_debt_reserve_ratio.value|pct}, the lowest of the filled quarters, against {trend_table.quarters-back-1.ratios.bad_debt_reserve_ratio.value|pct} in the prior quarter and {trend_table.quarters-back-4.ratios.bad_debt_reserve_ratio.value|pct} a year earlier, and the allowance balance fell within the quarter while receivables rose to their high. Fair-value accounting for acquired receivables dilutes the ratio but does not lower the balance; no item explains it, and no field carries the release, so no adjustment is written.

anomalies.name: Contingent consideration estimate cut adds a gain to operating expense
anomalies.name_ko: 조건부 대가 추정치 하향으로 영업비용 감소
anomalies.what: The company says "we reduced our estimate of future cash payments" under the QRadar arrangement, booking "a gain of $110 million for the change in fair value of contingent consideration liability" inside general and administrative expense; the cash-flow remeasurement line confirms a non-cash credit this year after a charge a year earlier. It lowers reported expense in a loss quarter; no calculator field carries the amount, so no earnings adjustment is written.

anomalies.name: Lower inventory obsolescence charges amid component shortages
anomalies.name_ko: 부품 부족 속 재고 진부화 비용 감소
anomalies.what: MD&A says product cost rose "partially offset by a decrease in inventory excess and obsolete charges" while also citing hardware demand and "supply chain disruptions, including increased memory, storage or other component shortages"; lower obsolescence charges raise product margin. The record tags no quarter-end inventory, no inventory reserve and no current-year write-down, so the reserve change cannot be checked.

anomalies.name: Long useful life on the largest acquired intangible
anomalies.what: The largest CyberArk intangible, platform renewals, carries a long useful life (item estimates_and_discretion_cyberark_platform_renewals_long_useful_life), longer than developed technology, which spreads its amortization thinly. Amortization still rose: year-to-date depreciation and amortization is {terms.trailing_four_quarters.depreciation_and_amortization.parts.this_year_to_date.value} against {terms.trailing_four_quarters.depreciation_and_amortization.parts.prior_year_to_date.value} a year earlier. A long life flatters future operating income if renewals decay faster.

anomalies.name: Acquisition allocations still open
anomalies.what: The CyberArk and Koi allocations remain in the measurement period, "which may result in changes to the amounts and allocations recorded"; goodwill and intangibles, now most of total assets, can still move, and no impairment test, headroom or assumption is in the input.

anomalies.name: Period-end note liability measured on post-period share prices
anomalies.name_ko: 분기말 이후 주가로 측정한 전환사채 부채
anomalies.what: The surrendered convertible notes are a current liability whose fair value was "estimated based on the sum of the daily conversion values computed from our stock price" over a window running past the balance-sheet date; the current convertible debt item matches the stated figure. The company had no such instrument before.

anomalies.name: Fair value option ties earnings to the share price
anomalies.what: The company elected the fair value option for the assumed notes and carries capped calls as derivatives, so "changes in fair value of 2030 Notes included in earnings were a loss of $37 million" and earnings now move with the share price; the derivative line shows the small capped-call loss the note describes. The only tagged other-income line is level with the year-ago quarter and total other income, net is not in the calculator, so where the note loss sits is unresolved.

anomalies.name: Tax expense on a pre-tax loss; base year carried a deferred tax benefit
anomalies.what: The note says "our provision for income taxes reflected an effective tax rate of negative" for the quarter and names CyberArk as a cause; year-to-date tax expense of {terms.trailing_four_quarters.income_tax_expense.parts.this_year_to_date.value} compares with {terms.trailing_four_quarters.income_tax_expense.parts.prior_year_to_date.value} a year earlier on lower pre-tax income, and the trailing effective rate is {tax_rate.effective_rate|pct}. The deferred income tax line swings from a large non-cash benefit in the prior-year nine months to a small charge, so the base year's income carried a tax benefit this year's does not; taxes run against reported income now.

anomalies.name: Tax-deductible acquired goodwill
anomalies.what: For CyberArk "Substantially all of goodwill is deductible for U.S. income tax purposes", and Koi's goodwill is deductible too, while book goodwill is not amortized, so cash taxes should run below book tax later. No income-taxes-payable line is in my input and the deferred tax balances moved for several reasons.

anomalies.name: Litigation accrual: base-year release and unaccrued European matters
anomalies.name_ko: 소송충당금: 전년 환입과 유럽 소송 미적립
anomalies.what: The accrual reads "we accrued $150 million and $146 million based on the judgment and estimated interest, which is recorded in other long-term liabilities"; the base-year nine months included a partial release that flattered fiscal 2025 general and administrative expense, and the European matters carry no accrual because "Those matters are still pending". Other non-current liabilities rose, consistent with the accrual; the release itself is not visible in the numbers.

anomalies.name: Soft assets at their high after CyberArk
anomalies.what: The soft-asset share is {trend_table.quarters-back-0.ratios.soft_asset_share.value|pct}, the highest of the filled quarters, against {trend_table.quarters-back-1.ratios.soft_asset_share.value|pct} in the prior quarter and {trend_table.years-back-1.ratios.soft_asset_share.value|pct} at the fiscal 2024 year end; total assets stepped up within the quarter with CyberArk goodwill and intangibles, as the allocation note says.

anomalies.name: Acquisition charges framed as near-term while acquisitions recur
anomalies.what: The quarter's operating result of {ratios.growth.operating_income.this_quarter.value} reflects the acquired businesses' "operating loss of $523 million and $524 million", acceleration where "we recorded share-based compensation of $177 million", transaction costs and severance, and management frames its expense outlook "Excluding the near-term impact of our recent acquisitions". Chronosphere, CyberArk and Koi closed within fiscal 2026 and Portkey closed after the quarter, so acquisition cost recurs; no non-GAAP measure is in my input to show how much is excluded.

anomalies.name: Gross margin at its quarterly low as acquired amortization enters cost of revenue
anomalies.name_ko: 인수 무형자산 상각으로 매출총이익률 분기 최저
anomalies.what: Quarter gross margin is {trend_table.quarters-back-0.ratios.gross_margin.value|pct}, the lowest of the filled quarters, against {trend_table.quarters-back-1.ratios.gross_margin.value|pct} in the prior quarter and {trend_table.quarters-back-4.ratios.gross_margin.value|pct} a year earlier; the notes attribute it to acquired-intangible amortization in both cost lines, tariffs and lower hardware margins. Costs are being recognised, not deferred.

anomalies.name: Other income carries one-off portfolio gains and new losses
anomalies.what: Other income in the first nine months was lifted by "increased gains on sales of our investments to fund acquisitions", with investment sales far above the prior-year nine months; the same line carries the convertible-note fair value loss and foreign currency losses larger than a year earlier. These are non-recurring in kind and are not separated in the calculator.

anomalies.name: Rising sales of financing receivables
anomalies.what: "We sold financing receivables of $49 million and $54 million" in the three and nine months, more than in the same periods of fiscal 2025; selling receivables turns future customer payments into current operating cash. The calculator's proceeds field is missing because the record tags no such proceeds, so the reducing adjustment written against it may carry no amount.

anomalies.name: Shrinking customer-financing book lifts operating cash flow
anomalies.what: Both financing-receivable balances fell between the fiscal year end and the quarter end and their operating cash-flow line is larger than a year earlier, while the trade-receivables line records {terms.trailing_four_quarters.change_in_receivables.parts.this_year_to_date.value} against {terms.trailing_four_quarters.change_in_receivables.parts.prior_year_to_date.value}, a smaller release. MD&A attributes the rise in year-to-date operating cash flow, from {terms.trailing_four_quarters.operating_cash_flow.parts.prior_year_to_date.value} to {terms.trailing_four_quarters.operating_cash_flow.parts.this_year_to_date.value}, to "growth of our business as reflected by increases in collections"; a shrinking financing book is a source that runs out, and the explanation does not name it.

anomalies.name: Off-balance-sheet purchase obligations rose steeply
anomalies.what: Unrecorded purchase obligations are {terms.balances_now.unconditional_purchase_obligations.value} against {terms.balances_a_year_earlier.unconditional_purchase_obligations.value} a year earlier, against trailing revenue growth of {ratios.growth.revenue.trailing_four_quarters.value|pct}. MD&A gives "our commitments to purchase products, components, cloud hosting and other services totaled $8.6 billion", mostly cloud hosting, and the note adds "a $92 million minimum purchase commitment with a cloud hosting service provider through September 2027 with no specified annual commitments".

anomalies.name: Calculator carries a stale, understated lease liability
anomalies.what: The headquarters amendments state "The amendments resulted in an increase of $262 million in our right-of-use assets in exchange for new operating lease liabilities", and right-of-use assets and non-current lease liabilities both rose; the calculator still carries the fiscal 2025 year-end total of {ratios.solvency.operating_lease_liability.value} because the quarter's filing tags no total, and it flags that the non-current part alone now exceeds it.

anomalies.name: Acquisition consideration paid through financing activities
anomalies.what: Contingent consideration paid to IBM appears in financing activities in the first nine months of fiscal 2026, against none a year earlier, and MD&A names it as a driver of financing cash use; paid there, it bypasses operating cash flow and the acquisitions line that quality-adjusted free cash flow subtracts. No calculator field carries the payment.

anomalies.name: Share-based compensation rising, with more already committed
anomalies.name_ko: 주식보상비용 증가 및 향후 비용 예정
anomalies.what: Share-based compensation is {terms.trailing_four_quarters.share_based_compensation.value} over the trailing four quarters against {earnings_versus_cash.history.years.0.share_based_compensation} in fiscal 2025; it includes acceleration where "we recorded share-based compensation of $177 million", and replacement awards keep it high because "The remaining fair value was allocated to future services and will be expensed over the remaining service periods as share-based compensation". It is a real cost already subtracted in quality-adjusted free cash flow.

anomalies.name: No control change reported in a very large acquisition quarter
anomalies.name_ko: 대규모 인수 분기에 내부통제 변화 없음 보고
anomalies.what: The controls section says "There were no changes in our internal control over financial reporting" in the quarter the company consolidated CyberArk and Koi, and does not mention integrating or excluding the acquired businesses' controls, though total assets stepped up within the quarter. No material weakness is reported, but no auditor's report or prior controls text is in my input.

anomalies.name: Calculator debt omits the assumed convertible notes
anomalies.what: The calculator's total debt is {ratios.solvency.total_debt.value} at the quarter end because its debt groups do not read the convertible-debt concepts, while the balance sheet carries current and non-current convertible debt and the notes describe the assumed CyberArk notes; calculator leverage, net debt and invested capital understate debt.

anomalies.name: Receivable cash-flow lines read with the wrong sign
anomalies.what: The numbers reader reads the negative trade-receivables and financing-receivables lines in the cash-flow statement as uses of cash; the calculator labels the receivables line as the increase in the asset, and both the trade and financing receivables balances fell between the fiscal year end and the quarter end, so those lines are releases of cash. The correction changes how operating cash flow is explained.

anomalies.name: Koi consideration described differently across filings
anomalies.what: The prior 10-Q's subsequent-event fact prints a Koi consideration figure for cash and replacement awards (item related_parties_contingencies_and_subsequent_events_note_koi_security_consideration); this 10-Q says "The total purchase consideration for the acquisition of Koi was $231 million" and that "we issued $61 million of replacement equity awards" allocated to future service. The bases differ and whether they reconcile is unresolved.

anomalies.name: MD&A commitments total above the note table
anomalies.name_ko: MD&A 구매약정 총액이 주석 표보다 큼
anomalies.what: MD&A says "our commitments to purchase products, components, cloud hosting and other services totaled $8.6 billion", above the note-table total the calculator carries at {terms.balances_now.unconditional_purchase_obligations.value}; the cloud-hosting minimum commitment stated outside the table is a candidate for the difference, which I do not compute.

anomalies.name: Capped-call cash possibly tagged as convertible-debt proceeds
anomalies.name_ko: 캡드콜 해지 현금이 전환사채 발행대금으로 태그됐을 가능성
anomalies.what: The notes say "In April 2026, we elected to terminate portions of the capped calls in exchange for $10 million in cash", and the only convertible-debt proceeds line carries the same amount, which the calculator counts as borrowing issued of {terms.cash_flow_families.borrowing_issued.value}; if the line is the capped-call cash, the calculator's net borrowing is misclassified.

anomalies.name: Distributor-concentrated receivables at a receivables high
anomalies.what: In fiscal 2025 the filing's distributor group held {concentration.facts.0.value|pct} of receivables and customers A, B and C held {concentration.facts.1.value|pct}, {concentration.facts.2.value|pct} and {concentration.facts.3.value|pct} of revenue; in the quarter receivables reached their high against revenue. With no current concentration fact, no channel inventory and no quarter-end inventory, whether sales were pushed into the channel cannot be tested.

adjustments.name: Sales of financing receivables lift operating cash flow
adjustments.quote: We sold financing receivables of $49 million and $54 million for the three and nine months ended April 30, 2026

summary_ko.earnings_versus_cash: 최근 연환산 기준 영업현금흐름은 순이익의 {earnings_versus_cash.operating_cash_flow_over_net_income.value}배로 직전 회계연도의 {earnings_versus_cash.history.years.0.operating_cash_flow_over_net_income}배보다 높아, 이익은 현금으로 충분히 뒷받침됩니다. 다만 매출채권 증가액 {earnings_versus_cash.working_capital.receivables.balance_sheet_change.value} 가운데 현금흐름표에 나타나지 않는 {earnings_versus_cash.working_capital.receivables.articulation_gap.value}는 인수로 들어온 채권일 가능성이 크지만 자료로 확인되지 않습니다.
summary_ko.revenue_recognition: 이번 분기 매출채권 회수기간은 {trend_table.quarters-back-0.ratios.days_sales_outstanding.value}일로 관측된 분기 중 가장 길고, 매출 대비 계약부채 비율은 {trend_table.quarters-back-0.ratios.contract_liabilities_over_revenue.value}로 가장 낮습니다. CyberArk 인수 시점 효과로 설명될 수 있지만, 새로 추가된 시점 인식 라이선스 매출과 함께 지켜봐야 할 신호입니다.
summary_ko.estimates_and_reserves: 대손충당금 비율이 {trend_table.quarters-back-0.ratios.bad_debt_reserve_ratio.value|pct}로 관측 분기 중 최저이고, QRadar 조건부 대가 추정치를 낮추면서 생긴 평가이익이 일반관리비를 줄였습니다. 반면 세금은 회사에 불리하게 움직여 연환산 유효세율이 {tax_rate.effective_rate|pct}입니다.
summary_ko.cost_deferral: 개발비 자본화는 없고 이연 판매수수료도 늘지 않았지만, 인수로 영업권과 무형자산이 늘어 연성자산 비중이 {trend_table.quarters-back-0.ratios.soft_asset_share.value|pct}로 최고입니다. 이번 분기 영업손익 {ratios.growth.operating_income.this_quarter.value}은 인수 관련 비용 때문인데, 회사는 이를 단기 영향으로 표현하지만 인수는 반복되고 있습니다.
summary_ko.cash_flow_engineering_and_off_balance_sh: 고객 금융채권의 매각과 잔액 감소가 영업현금흐름 증가의 일부를 만들었지만 MD&A는 이를 회수 증가로만 설명하며, 매각대금은 계산 파일에 태그되지 않아 조정 금액을 적용할 수 없습니다. 구매약정은 {terms.balances_a_year_earlier.unconditional_purchase_obligations.value}에서 {terms.balances_now.unconditional_purchase_obligations.value}로 늘었고, 주식보상비용 {terms.trailing_four_quarters.share_based_compensation.value}을 실제 비용으로 차감한 품질조정 잉여현금흐름은 {free_cash_flow.free_cash_flow_quality_adjusted.value}입니다.
summary_ko.controls_audit_and_filing_signals: 대규모 인수가 있었던 분기인데도 내부통제에 변화가 없다고만 밝히고 인수 회사 통제의 통합이나 평가 제외 여부를 언급하지 않았습니다. 감사인 보고서와 8-K 본문이 입력에 없어 감사인 교체, 임원 퇴임, 정정 공시 여부는 확인할 수 없습니다.
summary_ko.cross_document_reconciliation: 방향을 제시한 주석 항목 대부분은 숫자로 확인되었고 회사 자체 수치와 모순되는 항목은 없습니다. 다만 계산 파일의 총부채가 {ratios.solvency.total_debt.value}로 전환사채를 빠뜨렸고, Koi 인수대가 설명이 직전 분기 보고서와 다르며, 실적발표 8-K 본문이 없어 10-Q와 대조할 수 없습니다.
summary_ko.industry_lens: 분기말 재고 자료가 없어 재고 진부화를 측정할 수 없고, 재고 진부화 비용은 오히려 줄었습니다. 직전 회계연도에 유통업체 그룹이 매출채권의 {concentration.facts.0.value|pct}를 차지했고 이번 분기 매출채권이 최고 수준이라, 채널 밀어내기 여부는 확인되지 않은 채 남습니다.

limits: This analysis finds where the numbers and the explanations disagree, and where the company differs from its own past. It does not judge intent, and it cannot see evidence outside the filings, such as invoices or contracts.
